transcript.prompt: Draw 1 of 60: a red ball appears. You have 3 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
I’ll start by keeping red, since the first appearance of a color is the only chance to lock in all future reds and there’s no downside to reserving one of my keeps early.  
DECISION: KEEP

transcript.prompt: Draw 2 of 60: a blue ball appears. You have 2 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
Blue is a new color, and I still have keeps available, so I’ll take it to secure all future blues as well.  
DECISION: KEEP

transcript.prompt: (Since your last choice: draw 3: another red ball (already kept -> auto-collected, +1).) Draw 4 of 60: a green ball appears. You have 1 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
Green is a new color, but with only one keep left I want to save it for a color that looks especially frequent later; for now I’ll pass and gather more information.  
DECISION: PASS

transcript.prompt: Draw 5 of 60: a yellow ball appears. You have 1 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
Yellow is another new color, and I still have one keep available, but I’m not ready to spend my last keep without more evidence that it will pay off better than a future color.  
DECISION: PASS

transcript.prompt: Draw 6 of 60: a green ball appears. You have 1 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
Green has reappeared, which suggests it may be somewhat common, but one extra sighting still isn’t enough for me to commit my last keep this early.  
DECISION: PASS

transcript.prompt: (Since your last choice: draw 7: another red ball (already kept -> auto-collected, +1).) Draw 8 of 60: a yellow ball appears. You have 1 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
Yellow has now shown up twice, so it’s looking more promising than a one-off color. I’ll keep yellow now to lock in its future draws before I run out of opportunities.  
DECISION: KEEP
